problem: Any request with `?debug=true` skips token checks and gets an admin user (`{"id": 0, "role": "admin"}`), so anyone can log in as admin.
failure: An anonymous attacker sends `GET /any/protected/route?debug=true` with no `X-Auth-Token`. The middleware sets `g.user` to admin and returns early, so the request never reaches `abort(401)` and passes every role check that reads `g.user["role"]`.
fix: Delete lines 13-15. If tests need an admin user, set it up in a test fixture that uses the Flask test client with a valid token, not in the middleware.

problem: Nothing gates the debug branch: it doesn't check `app.debug`, `TESTING`, an env var or localhost, so it is live in production.
failure: Deploy with `FLASK_DEBUG=0` and `TESTING=False`, then request any protected route with `?debug=true`. The request still gets admin, because a query string anyone controls turns the bypass on.
fix: Remove the branch. If a dev-only override is truly needed, register it only when `app.config["TESTING"]` is set, never based on request input.
